Dossier 1: Small island state, sodomy laws on books but unenforced (2023 report), no LGR, no anti-discrimination, discrimination documented, no trans-specific violence data, no documented border treatment. Thin data. Sodomy statute unenforced → secondary. No trans-specific criminalisation documented, no documented targeting of trans visitors, no violence. Discrimination in public services documented. Constitution no equality clause. Thin data — extrapolate from structural facts: unenforced sodomy law, no protections, no record of relief, but also no record of enforcement. Score around 0.50-0.55. Fear of prosecution inhibits reporting — a real deterrent. But no documented trans-specific harm. I'd say ~0.52.

Dossier 2: Country with bathroom ban (2025) — universal exposure, tier 1 facility exclusion by birth sex, nationally imposed. Also anti-discrimination repeal attempt, hate crimes rising with trans women most affected, but also first conviction of police for torture of trans woman (17 years), court rulings against anti-equality decree, pride marches since 2002, conversion therapy ban, no criminalisation of trans identity. Bathroom restriction is universal exposure → tier 1. Rule of law shows some working for trans (conviction). But the bathroom ban applies to visitors in public restrooms. Score: universal exposure but with functioning recourse partially. ~0.50-0.55. Let's say 0.52.

Hmm, Dossier 1 vs Dossier 2: Dossier 2 has active universal exposure (bathroom law) plus documented rising hate crimes, but strong institutional responses. Dossier 1 has unenforced sodomy law, no documented trans-specific exposure, but no protections and discrimination documented. Rule 21: universal exposure without working remedy → Elevated band. The bathroom ban — remedy unclear. I'd put dossier 2 at ~0.50 and dossier 1 at ~0.55.

Dossier 3: Criminalises same-sex conduct (sodomy, 1 year), enforcement uncommon but exists — some LGBTQ arrested after attackers used status as excuse; deterrence from reporting. Active legislative push for harsher anti-gay bill. No gender-affirming care available. Public concealment norm. No documented trans-specific violence. Employment protection exists. Trans-specific care absence affects visitors needing refills — medication access. Score: criminalisation statute with some enforcement, active hostile legislative climate, concealment norm. ~0.40-0.45. Sodomy law applies to women too — a trans visitor could be caught if read as same-sex couple. Enforcement uncommon. I'd say 0.42.

Dossier 4: Regional union free movement (EU-like). No entry/documentation obstacle specific to trans. But: medicalised LGR, registry refusal — resident-facing. Legislative attempts to criminalise trans lives failed. Lethal attack on LGBT bar 2022 (2 killed) — single incident but a targeted attack, rights groups say new era. Official hostility from culture minister. Marriage ban, constitutional amendment. Hostile public opinion, low acceptance. No documented criminalisation of trans identity; failed bills. So worst feature: societal hostility + official statements, plus a lethal venue attack (2022, dated ~4 years). Also document regime: surgical sterilisation required, registry refusal — resident-facing, doesn't reach visitors (visitor uses home passport). No documented border friction.

So Dossier 4: no criminalisation, anti-discrimination law covering GI (a protection operating), but hostile climate, failed criminalisation bills, one lethal attack, official hostility. Public hostility tier 3, dated incident tier 4. I'd rate ~0.55-0.60. The anti-discrimination act covering provision of goods and services is traveler-relevant. But hostile public opinion and regressive trajectory. I'd say 0.57.

Hmm but the bathroom-like exposures? None documented. Rule of law — anti-discrimination enforcement unknown. The attack's aftermath: no progress, more at risk. I'd say 0.55.

Dossier 5: Criminalises same-sex relations (10-15 yrs), gender-affirming healthcare (1-3 yrs) — transition itself criminal; "promoting homosexuality"; deportation; no LGR; documented killings with impunity, UN says country is perpetrator; sectarian militia death squads targeting gender-nonconforming dress; targeted killing 2023. This is severe — near 0.10-0.15. Not execution by state per se, but documented pattern of killings with impunity + criminalisation of trans identity itself. Gender-affirming care criminalised — a trans visitor on HRT carries medication → criminal exposure. State-tolerated targeting. Score ~0.10.

Now Dossier 1 vs 3: Dossier 1 unenforced statute, no trans-specific record. Dossier 3 enforced somewhat (some arrests), active hostile legislation, concealment norm, no care access. Dossier 3 worse: ~0.42. Dossier 1: ~0.52.

Actually reconsider Dossier 1: fear of prosecution inhibits reporting to police, no constitutional protections, discrimination in public services, small island. But no documented trans-specific harm, statute unenforced. Also no data on border treatment — open question, not exposure. 0.50-0.55. I'll give 0.53.

Dossier 2: bathroom universal exposure. Also 2024 decreed transsexualism mental health (walked back), conversion therapy ban (positive), first torture conviction (positive, rule of law working for trans). Hate crimes rising, trans women most affected (sub-registry, no denominator → weak). Bathroom law national, universal exposure for travelers using public restrooms. Severity: restriction of facilities access = tier 1-ish (facility exclusion by birth sex). Rule 21 band implication: universal exposure without documented working remedy → Elevated band (0.40-0.60). So dossier 2 should be in elevated band. With strong institutional positives (court convictions, pride, no criminalisation), upper end: 0.50.

Dossier 4: hostile climate, official hostility, lethal attack but dated, anti-discrimination protections covering GI, no criminalisation, no universal exposure documented. Also 40% discrimination survey (2017, LGBT-wide, older → little weight). Probably 0.55. Is it above Dossier 2? Dossier 2 has a tier-1 universal exposure (bathroom ban); Dossier 4's worst is tier 3 societal hostility + dated tier-4 violence. Per precedence ladder, Dossier 4 should be above Dossier 2. So: D4 = 0.58, D2 = 0.50.

And Dossier 1 (0.53) — between them? Dossier 1's worst: unenforced sodomy statute (secondary, tier 5-ish/low), documented discrimination in public services (tier 3, thin recourse), no protections, no trans-specific violence. Should D1 sit above D2? D1 has no universal exposure, no documented targeting. But thin data and no relief record. Rule 13: latent tangential statute + open questions + thin formal recourse = a step below acceptance-with-protections tier. That's not directly applicable. I'd put D1 ~0.52, D2 ~0.50 — close. Let me differentiate: D2 has documented universal-exposure law; D1 doesn't. D1 discrimination in public services documented without recourse (tier 3). Hmm, both elevated. D1 = 0.52, D2 = 0.48.

Actually is D2's bathroom ban definitely in force? "A law enacted 13 May 2025 restricts trans people's use of public restrooms" — enacted; also April 2025 law mandates restroom restriction by biological sex. Deliberately not counted notes ambiguity about whether bills enacted... but the assessment says enacted 13 May 2025. Take it as in force. Universal exposure for travelers (hotels, restaurants, transit). Severity moderate-to-major (facility denial). Plus hostile framing (trans as harassment risk). I'd say 0.46-0.50. Given positives (convictions, courts, no criminalisation, conversion ban), 0.48.

Dossier 3: 0.40-0.45. Criminalisation with some enforcement, arrests of LGBTQ after attackers' claims, active harsher bills, concealment norm, no care. Employment protection (resident-facing). 0.42.

Final: 1: 0.52, 2: 0.48, 3: 0.42, 4: 0.58, 5: 0.10.

Fine.

D4 0.58 above D1 0.52? D4 has anti-discrimination law covering gender identity across goods/services (traveler-relevant), no criminalisation, free movement; but hostile public opinion, official hostility, failed criminalisation bills, lethal attack aftermath. D1: no protections, discrimination documented, sodomy statute unenforced, thin data. D4's positives stronger; D4's negatives (official hostility statements, societal hostility) tier 3. I'd keep D4 = 0.58, D1 = 0.52.
